# Spectral Analysis in Practice {#sec-spectral-analysis}

Real signals are long, and their spectra are continuous. This chapter turns the DFT into a practical tool.

::: {.callout-note}
## Draft chapter
This chapter is planned but not yet written. The outline below is the
working plan.
:::

## Planned contents

- From the DFT to the DTFT, intuitively
- Zero padding: prettier plots, no new information
- Windows and spectral leakage
- Time-frequency analysis: the spectrogram and the uncertainty trade-off
- Digital frequency vs. frequency in hertz
- Fourier series of a periodic continuous signal, built up numerically (square wave, Gibbs phenomenon)
- A bridge to the continuous-time Fourier transform, only at the level needed for sampling
